title: Scott Bessent - Macro Maven (EP.415)

meta.transcript source: YouTube auto-captions (no punctuation on this video's captions)

speakers: Scott Bessent (CEO/CIO Key Square Group, ex-Soros CIO, macro investor)
summary: Ted Seides interviews Scott Bessent on his path from Jim Rogers and Jim Chanos to Soros and Key Square. Approach: a few asymmetric, imagination-driven macro bets built from micro information, policy-change detection and P&L-based sizing, with strict liquidity and tail-risk rules. Views (Oct 2024): election-dependent growth shock, long gold, Japan bull, China stagnation, Le Pen in France.

coverage.note: intro, sponsor read, childhood; father's boom-bust leading to risk focus (no separate claim)
imagination as method (subprime), Jim Rogers research approach
Brown Brothers, Oman family option leverage, joining Chanos
short selling in 1988-91, policy overreaction, short alpha, leaving Chanos
Soros/Druckenmiller style: micro drives macro, instrument choice, correlation check, conviction, patience
Soros culture, British pound / ERM trade mechanics and asymmetry
Soros reflexivity trends, external manager model, instrument restriction mistake at Bessent Capital

allocator behaviour, SPVs, newspaper test, election/China/gold views, policy brick wall
policy personnel and entry points, Japan, Europe, political motivation, debt growth thesis, realignment
closing remarks and outro; nothing actionable

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I had the ability to imagine a different state of the world and believe it could happen
claims.claim: Big macro payoffs come from imagining a never-before-seen state of the world (e.g. a national US housing recession) and finding an instrument with asymmetric payoff that captures it.
claims.conditions: when consensus cannot conceive of the event
claims.testable: no - judgment about imagination, not a rule

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: he couldn't imagine that this could happen or that these tranches in the cdos could be wiped out
claims.claim: Experts anchored on history missed the subprime collapse because they could not imagine CDO tranches being wiped out; a respected mortgage manager was recommending mortgages mid-crisis and his fund fell 100%.
claims.conditions: when systemic risk has never occurred before

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: he always said that he was looking for major secular change it was dig dig dig can you prove it
claims.claim: Jim Rogers method: look for major secular change and test whether the numbers match the story before acting (research, research, research).
claims.testable: partly - 'numbers match the story' can be checked case by case

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: you could Goose the returns with leverage with options
claims.claim: For concentrated long-term investors the same stock views can be enhanced with leverage and options, so there are many ways to express one investment idea.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: a lot of times when there is a bad reaction you get an equal and opposite misguided reaction on the other side
claims.claim: Bad policy creates good opportunities: after the S&L bust a regulator overreacted with supervisory tightening (write down even current loans), producing an opposite misguided reaction and mispriced bank stocks.
claims.conditions: when regulators panic after a crisis
claims.testable: partly - policy-overreaction episodes can be studied

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the value added was could you be in something that could go to zero
claims.claim: A short book adds alpha beyond market beta and industry group by holding stocks that can go to zero; in 1990 shorts were up 50% while the S&P fell high teens to 20%.
claims.direction: short individual names that can go to zero
claims.conditions: bear markets with fraud/leverage unwinds

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: AUM chases performance so everyone wanted to be short
claims.claim: Assets arrive after the strategy has already performed (short fund grew from $37M to $500M) and opportunities then run out (could not find anything to short), so capital inflows lag opportunity.
claims.conditions: after a strong run for a strategy

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the micro drives the macro so we can get a huge amount of information from what companies are telling us
claims.claim: Bottom-up company information is a better macro input than forecasting macro aggregates directly; individual forecasts of PCE deflator or leading indicators cannot beat the crowd.
claims.conditions: when company statements are read across many sectors
claims.testable: partly - corporate guidance/earnings-call text signals can be tested

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: if trucking companies are telling you the business is taking off then that's very interesting
claims.claim: Specific company read-throughs (trucking demand, Home Depot supply shortages, bank CEOs reporting souring credit cards) give early macro direction on activity and credit.
claims.indicator: trucking, retail, bank credit card commentary

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: where can you get the most bang for the buck so if you think oil's going up if drilling stocks are really beaten down then maybe it's stuck
claims.claim: Once a view is formed choose the instrument with the best payoff: stocks, futures curve (forward curve may predict decline) or options, depending on what the market is pricing.
claims.indicator: oil forward curve, drilling stocks, options
claims.direction: pick cheapest expression of the view
claims.testable: partly - cross-instrument payoff comparison is possible

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the risk manager would do a correlation and it had a 98% r squared with the S&P
claims.claim: Before sizing a new idea check its correlation to the existing book: an apparently unique idea (e.g. in Australia) can be 98% R-squared with the S&P, i.e. just alternate beta.
claims.conditions: when idea sold as diversifying

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: George Soros has this famous saying I just need enough information to make a decision he does not have analysis paralysis
claims.claim: Conviction should build as confidence rises (Druckenmiller: above the 50th percentile of confidence, grow the position) while avoiding analysis paralysis.
claims.testable: partly - confidence-based sizing is hard to measure

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: he said I only swing at strikes
claims.claim: Concentration with high conviction means you may sit in cash until a fat pitch appears (Ted Williams: only swing at strikes).
claims.direction: hold cash when no high-quality idea
claims.testable: partly - selectivity vs hit rate can be tested

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: if the bank of England raised rates on Wednesday mortgages went up on Friday
claims.claim: UK mortgages floated with the base rate, so defending the pound in the ERM by raising rates would bankrupt the voting public; the policy was therefore politically unsustainable and the British and German rate needs were incompatible.
claims.conditions: when a currency peg forces rates against domestic conditions
claims.testable: partly - pegs under domestic pain can be screened historically

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the most they could push us back was 2 and a half% and if the corridor broke we can make whatever in a day
claims.claim: The ERM pound short was asymmetric: the band capped the loss at about 2.5% while a break paid very large amounts in a day, and the authorities had to buy unlimited pounds to defend it.
claims.conditions: when a peg/band with limited downside for the bettor
claims.testable: partly - payoff of band-break trades can be tested

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: he would add a 300% position because things really used to Trend a lot more
claims.claim: In the 1980s currency realignments (Plaza, Louvre) moved 6% in a night and trends were stronger, so Soros added huge positions into winners; the 'real-time experiment' journal year returned over 140%.
claims.conditions: when policy-driven realignments occur; speaker says trends were stronger then
claims.testable: partly - trend strength over eras is testable

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: great manager would be someone who one two three times a year maybe only every other year would come say this is a big trade idea
claims.claim: A good external manager is one you never worry about; a great one brings a big trade idea a few times a year or proposes an SPV, so the core team can leverage its knowledge through specialist managers.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: never do what the investors tell you to do do what you're good at
claims.claim: Restricting a macro investor to long/short equities (at investors' request in 2000) lost asymmetry and hurt results; use the fund's true skill and full instrument set.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the oil stocks didn't move because they were looking more at the mid curve
claims.claim: When oil rose, oil equities did not follow because they price off the mid-curve and analyst price decks, so owning crude directly captures a bullish oil view better than oil stocks.
claims.indicator: oil spot vs oil equities / mid curve
claims.direction: long crude rather than oil stocks
claims.conditions: when spot moves but long-dated curve does not
claims.testable: yes - spot-vs-equity beta can be tested

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: rather than size being the enemy of performance whether you could turn size free form Capital so no mandate and the ability to make quick decisions into an asset
claims.claim: Large capital can be an advantage if it is unconstrained and decisions are fast (answer in three days versus an investment committee with five memos in three weeks).
claims.conditions: free-form mandate, no committee

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the Hub and spoke system for the external managers was very successful
claims.claim: A hub-and-spoke model (small internal core team plus outside managers who bring ideas without being bigfooted) worked well at scale.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: John corzine's firm got liquidated out of their Italian Bond position and it was a three and a half billion dollar trade
claims.claim: In Sept 2011 a forced liquidation (MF Global) of Italian bonds let Soros take the whole $3.5bn trade with repo from JP Morgan, showing that large liquid capital earns by absorbing forced sellers.
claims.conditions: when a large holder is liquidated in a sovereign debt crisis
claims.testable: partly - forced-selling events can be studied

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: it's a real challenge as we get older to not become more negative all the time
claims.claim: Investors tend to become more negative with age, which must be actively resisted.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the liquid markets game or cards and back gamon it is luck and how are you going to manage the hand your dealt
claims.claim: Liquid markets resemble cards and backgammon rather than chess: events (Israel, Taiwan drills) are dealt randomly and success comes from managing what arrives, unlike private equity where all moves are on the board.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we just wanted to have a couple big positions manage them well and pick out the big themes try to keep the noise out
claims.claim: Key Square runs a few large positions on big themes with a small team plus about 30 regional consultants rather than local offices.
claims.testable: partly - concentration vs return can be tested

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the Yen had become the most expensive purchasing power parody currency in the world
claims.claim: Setup for the 2012-13 yen short: yen was the most overvalued currency on PPP after years of disinflation while Abe's three-arrow plan targeted 2% inflation, 2% growth in two years.
claims.conditions: when an extremely overvalued currency meets a credible policy regime change
claims.testable: yes - PPP valuation plus policy regime change is testable

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: he was able to reconstitute the board in His image
claims.claim: Conviction in the Abenomics trade came from verifying the mechanism: Abe could reconstitute the Bank of Japan board and get a reflationary governor, making the policy change feasible.
claims.conditions: when the political actor controls the central bank appointment process

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: it was very clear to me that the Yen was the ultimate expression and that equities would be a good derivative of that
claims.claim: Expressing a reflation view: the yen is the cleanest trade, with Japanese equities a derivative; avoid shorting JGBs (widowmaker) because JGB yields might fall before rising.
claims.direction: short JPY, long Japanese equities, avoid short JGBs
claims.conditions: when currency depreciation drives equities (exporters)

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we set up the fundamental picture so this is what could happen to the current account this is how cheap the currency is
claims.claim: Macro conviction process: lay out fundamentals (current account, valuation versus historical level), give reference points for potential, then add technicals such as exporter positioning and possible cascades.
claims.indicator: current account, currency valuation vs history
claims.testable: partly - valuation plus flows can be tested

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I think it's Nim Tob who says that lack of volatility leads to volatility
claims.claim: Low volatility lets positions build up, so a big regime change after a calm period can cascade; check where the market is positioned.
claims.conditions: after long low-vol periods

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we have this Vault fund that will sell you all the Yen puts you want
claims.claim: Options were cheap because yen vol was around 4-6 and a vol fund sold them thinking the buyer was crazy; buying options when vol is low and the thesis is a regime break offers asymmetric payoff.
claims.conditions: when implied vol is low relative to potential policy-driven move
claims.testable: yes - option payoff vs vol level can be tested

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I thought maybe it could go to 95 and then when this thing got in motion maybe it could go to 105
claims.claim: Price targets were stepped up as the move developed (78-82 range to 95, then 105, 115) rather than fixed in advance.
claims.direction: short JPY, raise targets as trend develops
claims.conditions: once the trade is in motion

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: the polic decision doesn't have to work but it can cause a lot of price gation
claims.claim: A policy regime change does not need to succeed to create a large price move; the market reaction itself is the trade (the market of the lifetime).
claims.conditions: when policy shifts are large and surprising

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I tend to trade in thirds and a lot of the position sizing is what's the market giving you
claims.claim: Build positions in thirds and size according to what the market offers, e.g. vol-implied asymmetry in options.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: adding if the p&l is good so that's a very different notion than a lot of people think about say fundamental investing
claims.claim: Add to winners when the year's P&L is good: position size is set by P&L cushion rather than only by conviction as in fundamental investing.
claims.testable: yes - P&L-conditioned sizing can be simulated

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: you earn the right to take a risk
claims.claim: Risk-taking capacity follows chip stack: bet more when you have more capital in hand for the year (like poker or backgammon, Annie Duke thinking in bets).
claims.testable: yes - risk budget tied to P&L

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: reset the chip stack
claims.claim: Reset the risk budget on January 1; taking profits in December on trending currencies usually proved right because there is always a counter-trend move.
claims.direction: reduce winning FX positions in mid-December
claims.conditions: year-end for strongly trending currencies
claims.testable: yes - December de-risking vs January returns is testable

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I'm a big believer in Nim tb's definition of risk probability and severity
claims.claim: Define risk as probability times severity, not volatility: e.g. China holds a small chance of a Russia-style day (equities down 95% in a day).
claims.conditions: for assets with jump/expropriation risk
claims.testable: partly - tail severity can be estimated

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: one of my risk management techniques have been you can be one thing but not many
claims.claim: Liquidity rule: be concentrated, illiquid or leveraged but never all three; prefer liquid and use leverage, and be able to exit part of the portfolio in 24-72 hours.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: a lot of macro tends to be more Babe Ruth than Ted Williams
claims.claim: Macro returns come from big home runs with a low batting average, so investors get impatient, redeem, and then return after strong years; this makes the business hard to sustain.
claims.testable: partly - macro return distribution is testable

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: when a manager has one two three blow it out of the park years you pull in some Capital pull it back and when they are in a slump you add
claims.claim: Per a Common Fund study, allocators do best trimming managers after strong years and adding during slumps.
claims.direction: trim after outperformance, add after slumps
claims.conditions: when you believe in the manager
claims.testable: partly - cited study, not verified here

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we create an SPV and can leverage up into the situation and then when that opportun passes we give the money back
claims.claim: Offer larger investors episodic SPVs for big ideas (once a year to once in three years) and return the capital when the opportunity ends.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: if IID had the real newspaper would it have been obvious what the trade is
claims.claim: Knowing future headlines does not give the trade: war in Israel with lower oil, or a 7% deficit with higher rates yet a tech bubble, show that mapping events to prices is unobvious.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: if Republicans which I'm pulling for it get the trifecta I think there could be a growth shock and animal Spirits are back
claims.claim: Oct 2024 view: a Republican sweep means a growth shock and animal spirits, making the Fed's jumbo cut a mistake and risking hikes; divided government under Harris leaves a 7% deficit unresolved.
claims.indicator: US election outcome, Fed cut, deficit
claims.conditions: depends on election result

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: he's a leninist so he's not going to allow a clearing function in the market
claims.claim: China: tactical stabilisation only; Xi is a Leninist who will not allow market clearing, so no sustainable Chinese economy.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I think we are in a long-term bull market in Gold I think we're seeing Reserve accumulation by central banks
claims.claim: Long gold, his biggest position, because central banks are accumulating reserves (Poland aiming for 20% gold).
claims.testable: yes - central bank purchases vs gold returns is testable

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: when a policy when a government when a management is driving 90 M an hour at a brick wall you assume that they are going to hit the brakes
claims.claim: Best investments detect when authorities will reverse an unsustainable policy; assume they brake before the wall (though sometimes they hit it).
claims.conditions: when a policy is clearly unsustainable
claims.testable: partly - identifying unsustainable policies is judgmental

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: they are very susceptible to external pressure
claims.claim: Policy is personnel: policymakers want to be judged well and are open to external pressure, so watching them over time makes it easy to anticipate when they slam the brakes.
claims.conditions: when policymakers are elected or reputation-driven

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: something has gone so far out of equilibrium you get a very good entry point
claims.claim: Anticipated policy brakes are also a risk-control metric because extremes that force a response give very good entry points.
claims.conditions: when policy reaction is likely
claims.testable: partly - extremes before reversal can be tested

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I believe that this could be a secular bull market one of the few in the world
claims.claim: Oct 2024 view: Japan could be a secular bull market after Abe's policies and stability, now at risk from prime minister turnover.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: I would predict that in the next 18 or 24 months Marine Le Pen the B Noir of European politics is going to be president of France
claims.claim: Europe is a policy question mark: populist backlash against trade and immigration plus German industrial policy mistakes (China sales, Russian energy, cheap currency, nuclear shutdown).

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we are going to decide whether we are going to grow our way out of this debt burden
claims.claim: US debt can be outgrown via deregulation, energy independence and a growth mindset; this is described as the last chance.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: we're in the midst of a great realignment and of a Britain Woods realignments coming in terms of global policy global trade
claims.claim: A Bretton Woods-type realignment of global policy and trade is coming.

claims.speaker: Scott Bessent
claims.quote: you have to believe that anything can happen you never know how things are going to change you got to be ready when they change
claims.claim: Prepare ahead and assume anything can happen so you are ready when a large event arrives (be prepared to get lucky).
